reading.statement: ⭐ the optimistic bound clears V1's bar at: 12 — NECESSARY, not sufficient (the K6 leak squeeze above still applies)
reading.THE_FINDING: ⭐⭐ THE TIER-ii ORGANIZER QUESTION IS SQUEEZED SHUT FROM BOTH ENDS. Below, the CEILING is too low: at d_addr=4 the best bijective re-placement gives 1.316 of 4 wells and an optimistic exact-set of 0.0117, 4.3x under V1's 0.0504 bar. Above, the PLACEMENT HEADROOM vanishes: ceiling-minus-identity falls 0.0851 -> 0.0375 -> 0.0109 -> 0.0000 across d_addr 4/6/8/12, and at d_addr=12 the launch head's OWN identity assignment is already the optimal bijection on 5/5 seeds. ⇒ the first d_addr whose ceiling clears the bar (12) is also the first at which a placement organizer has NOTHING LEFT TO DO. ⛔ Raising d_addr does not open the tier-ii question on this read protocol; it trades one reason it cannot be asked for another.
reading.caveat_on_the_finding: ⚠ NECESSARY-not-sufficient still binds, and a THIRD squeeze is UNMEASURED: spoke A measured the K6 query-only leak at 0.0007 (d=4) -> 0.5273 (d=16) -> 0.9844 (d=32) and NEVER AT d=12. So d=12's leak is a DECLARED UNKNOWN, not a clearance. ⛔ No arm was scored at any d in this probe.

caveats: ⛔ The ceiling is the best BIJECTIVE re-assignment of wells to cue sites — the MOST any placement organizer can achieve. It is an upper bound, not an arm's score.
⛔ optimistic_exact_set_* assumes independence across the F channels, which they do not satisfy; it is an UPPER bound on an UPPER bound and is out-of-class.

⚠ Raising d_addr is SQUEEZED FROM THE OTHER SIDE: spoke A measured K6 = 0.0007 (d=4) -> 0.5273 (d=16) -> 0.9844 (d=32) — at d >= 16 the launch head answers the family by itself. A ceiling that clears the bar is necessary, NOT sufficient.
⚠ C2W5's SP-2a measured the d-window EMPTY under the OLD launch protocol; this probe is on feature-factored launches and does not inherit that verdict either way.
⛔ This is a CONFIG INPUT, not a result: no store is built, no arm is scored, and no VALUE number exists anywhere in this file.
